questions.question: Name the five stages of the Technology design process and state what happens in each.
questions.expected_answer: Investigate: find out about the problem, the users, the context and existing solutions. Design: write a design brief with specifications and constraints, sketch possible ideas and choose the best. Make: build the model or product from a plan, using tools safely. Evaluate: test the product against the specifications and suggest improvements. Communicate: present the work with drawings, a model and a talk or report.

questions.question: List the five forces that can act on a structural member, and state what a gear ratio tells you about a pair of spur gears.
questions.expected_answer: Tension pulls a member longer; compression pushes it shorter; bending curves a beam, with tension on one face and compression on the other; torsion twists; shear slides one part across another. The gear ratio, driven teeth divided by driver teeth, tells you how many turns the driver makes for one turn of the driven gear; a ratio above 1 means the output turns more slowly with more turning force, a ratio below 1 means faster with less force.

questions.question: Explain the purpose of the baseline assessment and describe an effective way to prepare for it.
questions.expected_answer: The baseline is a short diagnostic task in the first week that does not count towards the mark. It shows the teacher and the learner which Grade 8 ideas are solid and which have gaps, so revision can be planned before the content is needed in a PAT. Effective preparation is active recall: cover the page, reproduce the idea from memory, check, and practise one example of each skill such as a circuit diagram, a gear ratio and the line conventions, rather than rereading.
